body.heading: Start your collection
paragraphs: With your adult, collect a few empty shells and smooth stones from a safe shore, or use shells and stones you already have at home.
Only take shells that are empty and dry. If something lives inside, it stays. Wash your hands after handling anything from the beach.

body.heading: Sort them your way
paragraphs: Sort your treasures into groups. You could sort by colour, by size, by shape, or by smooth and bumpy.
There is no single right way. Scientists sort things in different ways depending on what they want to find out. Your way is a real way.

body.heading: Make a pattern
paragraphs: Line your shells and stones up in a pattern: shell, stone, shell, stone. Then try a harder one: shell, shell, stone, shell, shell, stone.
Ask your adult to guess what comes next in your pattern. Then swap, and guess theirs.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: collect, sort, and line up shells and stones in your own patterns.

safetyNotes: Only collect empty shells with your adult, leave living creatures where they are, and wash hands after handling beach finds.
Stay with your adult near water, and never go into the sea to reach a shell or stone.

takeaway: Sorting the same treasures in different ways shows you something new each time.
